what: Yum China operates KFC and Pizza Hut in mainland China, where it has the exclusive licence to those brands, plus Lavazza coffee and several local formats. It runs more than 17,000 restaurants.
customers: Chinese consumers eating in restaurants, ordering delivery and buying coffee.
money: fried chicken restaurants, by far the biggest Western chain in China
Lavazza, Little Sheep and Huang Ji Huang
moat: The exclusive right to operate KFC in a market where it is the largest and most familiar Western restaurant chain, with supply chain and delivery infrastructure built over thirty years.
risks: Chinese consumer spending has been weak and customers have traded down
Revenue grew only about 4% last year
Price competition in Chinese fast food has intensified
Geopolitical sentiment can affect Western brands in China
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 12% with cash roughly matching debt
It keeps opening restaurants in smaller Chinese cities at low cost per store
Analysts see about 24% upside from current levels
watch: Same-store sales and new restaurant openings in lower-tier cities.
